title: Replay Timeline + Triage Guardrails: notes and wireframe
body:
Context and goal:
- Problem: Operators and SREs need a fast, structured way to understand intermittent timeouts, 5xx bursts, and model-origin errors (tokenization failures, invalid logits) across the Redwood Console. Current traces are too noisy and don’t help triage nondeterministic model failures.
- Goal: Add a replay-centric timeline + guardrails UX that: (1) surfaces error fingerprints and likely root causes, (2) lets engineers 'replay' a request with trace-level toggles (inject latency, change model variant, enable/disable cache), (3) provides suggested triage steps and automated runbook links.

High level concept:
- Left rail: event list (chronological) with compact badges (timeout, 5xx, model-error, partial-response). Each event row collapses to show request metadata (route, model, region, user id hash, token count, kv cache hit %). Hover shows a short error fingerprint: e.g., "prefix-match timeout at step 1.4s, no KV hit".
- Center: replay timeline (playhead) showing per-stage durations: router -> queue -> runtime(+kernel) -> model step -> post-proc. Visual stacked bars, color-coded by latency category (green < 100ms, amber 100-500ms, red >500ms).
- Right panel: inspector and triage actions. Tabs: "Request snapshot", "Token waterfall", "KV cache view", "Suggested fixes".
- Bottom: replay controls. Buttons: "Replay locally" (devbox), "Replay in sandbox" (isolated infra), "Replay with model-variant", toggles for: inject_delay(ms), disable_cache, use_quantized. Replay runs produce ephemeral logs and a diff view comparing original vs replay outputs.

Wireframe notes (low-fi):
- Event list row fields: timestamp | severity badge | route | model | latency | tokens | brief message. Click expands to show full raw request payload and response.
- Timeline: zoomable. Click on stack segment to surface the span logs from that layer. Right-click span -> "Open logs in Log Explorer" (links to logs).
- Token waterfall: show generation times per token for last N tokens (heatmap), highlight token-level model errors (e.g., invalid token returned). Also surface attention blowups: token probabilities that are extremely low/high relative to baseline.
- Suggested fixes algorithm (prototype rules):
  - If queue time >50% of total latency -> "Investigate routing/autoscale; consider Dedicated route or bump burst capacity"
  - If KV cache hit rate < 20% and prefix identical across requests -> "Enable prefix caching; add cache key rule"
  - If runtime kernel spin > 70% on specific GPU model -> "Flag serving-runtime perf regression, attach kernel profile"
  - If model emits repeated special-token or invalid-token sequences -> "Model-origin error: try model-variant stable-2024-11 or lower temperature; file ticket against model onboarding"

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can open an event and see timeline + per-span durations (console shows at least router, queue, runtime, model, postproc).
- Replay controls allow toggling: inject_delay, disable_cache, and choose a model variant and run a sandbox replay.
- Suggested fixes panel surfaces at least 4 automated rules with links to runbooks or tickets.
- Token waterfall available for requests <= 2048 tokens; waterfall view logs token generation times.

Telemetry signals to capture for evaluation:
- Click-through rate on suggested fixes (did user run suggested action)
- Replay success rate (replay completed without infra errors) and delta in latency/outputs vs original
- Time-to-triage: time from event opened -> ticket created or runbook executed
- Which rules are most frequently surfaced and accepted

Backlog grooming (items, priority, est):
- RED-3567: Basic timeline + event list (P0, 3 wk)
- RED-3571: Sandbox replay backend + api for ephemeral runs (P0, 4 wk)
- RED-3580: Token waterfall component + heatmap (P1, 2 wk)
- RED-3589: Suggested fixes rules engine + runbook linking (P1, 2 wk)
- RED-3595: Model-fingerprint classification service (cluster-level) for model-origin errors (P2, 3 wk)
- RED-3602: Integrate with A/B rollouts for automatic fallback policies from UI (P2, 3 wk)

Mockup copy/text samples (to use in hi-fi designs):
- "Request snapshot (id: rq_8f3a) — route: /v1/generate — user bucket: corp-prod — model: mixtral-8b-2025-01 (variant: quant-8)"
- "Fingerprint: repeated-early-timeout (sample rate: 12%) — likely cause: router backpressure or regional capacity fluctuation"
- Suggested fix pill examples: [Run in sandbox] [Disable prefix caching] [Switch to model variant: mixtral-8b-2024-stable]

Open questions / design decisions:
- Where to store ephemeral replay results and for how long? default TTL 48h? (cost implication)
- Should replay be limited by user tier? (Dedicated customers -> unlimited sandbox runs; hosted free-tier -> limited)
- How to represent nondeterministic model diffs in a small UI? (inline diff vs side-by-side vs scored similarity)
- Level of access control for replay: do we require additional permissions to run with 'disable_cache' or 'inject_delay'?

Implementation notes for eng teams:
- Backend: expose an endpoint /admin/replay that accepts the original request blob + modifiers, returns ephemeral run id. Keep replay infra isolated (sandbox pool) to avoid capacity noisy neighbors.
- Instrumentation: ensure per-span ids are stable and propagate KV-cache hit metric. Add lightweight profiling to runtime to produce kernel-level CPU/GPU time per inference step.
- Data retention: ephemeral runs stored in S3 with folder per tenant, TTL policy and manual 'save as trace' option that promotes to longterm storage with audit log.

Next steps / action items:
- UX: produce hi-fi wireframes for left rail event list + center timeline (owner: Liam) — due 2025-02-10
- Eng infra: prototype sandbox replay API and secure it behind feature flag (owner: Arjun) — spike due 2025-02-14
- Product: prioritize rule-set for suggested fixes and map to existing runbooks (owner: Maya) — review 2025-02-07

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally replay-first, not log-first; idea is to make triage a short 'change + replay' loop.
- Keep language conservative for production-facing copy: emphasize "sandbox" and "ephemeral" so customers understand cost and retention tradeoffs.

Rough ascii layout for designers:
[ Left rail: event list ] | [ Center: replay timeline -> stacked spans ] | [ Right: inspector tabs ]
- Bottom-toolbar: [Replay: Sandbox] [Replay: Local] [Compare outputs] [Create ticket]

Examples / mini-scenarios (to include in test playbook):
- Scenario A: Bursty 5xxs — timeline shows runtime kernel spinup spikes; replay with quantized = no improvement -> assign to serving-runtime perf team.
- Scenario B: Intermittent timeouts for long prefix prompts — low KV hits; replay with disable_cache=False vs True shows latency regression when cache disabled -> root cause: malformed cache key generation in client.
- Scenario C: Model-origin artifact — model emits invalid-token sequence; replay with model-variant=stable-2024 reproduces. Create model onboarding ticket and block auto-upgrade.

Appendix: quick links for reference:
- Existing Log Explorer spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/log-explorer-spec
- Prior art: Sentry replay + Datadog Live Session examples (used for interaction patterns)

End of doc.
